answer: The protocol requires each agent to secure 1,000 unique capacity-reservations from a centralized issuer, treating the allocation as a secure haven for computation. A verifier emits pulse tests through a copper-wired path to ensure exclusivity. If an agent fails to maintain its slot or uses a relay, it forfeits its fee. Honest agents pay 1x cost, while attackers pay 1,000x for separate slots. The walnut-sized latency buffer prevents pooling.
